raw_case_text:
A 54-year-old woman presented to our emergency department complaining of fever, chills, rigors, diarrhea, and upper abdominal discomfort. In July 2017, she received a diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma treated with a total pancreatectomy with regional lymph node dissection. The post-operative pathology report described the tumor as being a stage T2 N1 M0 - grade 2 malignancy, and synchronous adjuvant chemotherapy and radiotherapy were performed. Adjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine plus cisplatin for 4 cycles were completed in November 2017. Her physical examination revealed right upper quadrant tenderness and ascites. Laboratory studies showed an increased C-reactive protein level of 107.67 mg/L (normal range, 0-8 mg/L), leukocytosis with a white blood cell count of 11.31x10/L (normal range, [4.2-10.2]x10/L), low platelet count of 54x10/L (normal range, 142-424x10/L). Liver enzyme levels were also elevated including aspartate aminotransferase (43 U/L: normal range <32 U/L), alkaline phosphatase (192-32 U/L: normal range: 40-150 U/L), a gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase (172 U/L: normal range: 5-39 U/L), and lactate dehydrogenase (519 U/L: normal range: 125-243 U/L). Serum total and direct bilirubin levels were elevated, with values of 0.58 mg/dL (normal range: 0-0.5 mg/dL) and 1.60 mg/dL (normal range: 0.2-1.2 mg/dL), respectively. Tests for amebiasis, Clostridium difficile infections, hepatitis viruses were negative, but blood cultures for Fusobacterium necrophorum were positive. No invasive procedure was applied to the patient during this period. Meanwhile, the patient was not receiving any medical oncology treatment. MRI of the abdomen revealed multiple intrahepatic abscesses in addition to pylephlebitis in the intrahepatic branches of the portal vein (Figures 1-2). The patient was successfully treated with intravenous (IV) cefaperazone-sulbactam (2 gr/day) for 10 days and both her clinical and laboratory findings showed improvement. Follow-up MRI revealed the resolution of the liver abscesses and pylephlebitis. Furthermore, the 18F-FDG PET/CT results showed absence of FDG uptake elsewhere in the body (Figure 3).
This report does not contain any personal information that could lead to the identification of the patient and the personal details of the patient were excluded. A written informed consent from the patient is included in this article.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 54-year-old woman with a history of resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma presented to the emergency department with fever, chills, rigors, diarrhea, and upper abdominal discomfort.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with acute fever, chills, rigors, diarrhea, and upper abdominal discomfort. She had undergone total pancreatectomy with regional lymphadenectomy in July 2017 for stage T2N1M0 (grade 2) pancreatic adenocarcinoma followed by chemoradiotherapy and 4 cycles of adjuvant gemcitabine plus cisplatin completed in November 2017, and was off active oncologic therapy with no recent invasive procedures at the time of presentation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Stage T2N1M0 grade 2 pancreatic adenocarcinoma status post total pancreatectomy with regional lymph node dissection (July 2017) and adjuvant chemoradiotherapy plus 4 cycles of gemcitabine/cisplatin (completed November 2017).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, chills, rigors, diarrhea, and upper abdominal discomfort.

objective.physical_examination: Abdominal examination revealed right upper quadrant tenderness and clinical ascites.
objective.routine_investigations: Laboratory studies: elevated CRP 107.67 mg/L (normal 0-8 mg/L), leukocytosis with WBC 11.31 x 10^9/L (normal 4.2-10.2 x 10^9/L), thrombocytopenia with platelets 54 x 10^9/L (normal 142-424 x 10^9/L), AST 43 U/L (normal <32 U/L), ALP 192.32 U/L (normal 40-150 U/L), GGT 172 U/L (normal 5-39 U/L), LDH 519 U/L (normal 125-243 U/L), direct bilirubin 0.58 mg/dL (normal 0-0.5 mg/dL), and total bilirubin 1.60 mg/dL (normal 0.2-1.2 mg/dL). Diagnostic tests for amebiasis, Clostridium difficile infection, and viral hepatitis were all negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal MRI demonstrated multiple intrahepatic abscesses accompanied by pylephlebitis (septic thrombosis) of the intrahepatic portal vein branches. Follow-up 18F-FDG PET/CT showed no abnormal FDG-avid metastatic recurrence elsewhere in the body.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Peripheral blood cultures grew Fusobacterium necrophorum (while amebiasis, Clostridium difficile, viral hepatitis, and tumor recurrence on 18F-FDG PET/CT were excluded), confirming Fusobacterium necrophorum bacteremia complicated by multiple pyogenic liver abscesses and intrahepatic portal vein pylephlebitis. The patient was treated with intravenous cefoperazone-sulbactam 2 g/day for 10 days, resulting in clinical and biochemical recovery and complete resolution of both the hepatic abscesses and pylephlebitis on follow-up abdominal MRI.
